item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is materially closer to the frozen contract because it adds the required replayable Upload API while preserving FilesService.Add’s existing behavior. A makes an explicitly out-of-scope behavioral change to Add.","reasons":["B uses internal/multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\", validates empty filenames and nil content, and preserves FilesOption handling and response/error semantics.","B leaves Add unchanged, whereas A eagerly reads and buffers every Add body, changing memory use, reader-error timing/semantics, and the documented low-level API behavior.","A’s changelog and README explicitly promise replayability for caller-encoded Add bodies, contradicting the contract’s direction not to change Add or retry machinery.","B retains the existing Add test and adds focused multipart and retry tests. A replaces the basic Add test and adds behavior the contract did not request or permit."],"risks_a":["Upload calls a new private add helper rather than routing through FilesService.Add, violating the explicit reuse requirement.","Changing Add to io.ReadAll can impose substantial memory costs on custom multipart bodies and wraps new source-reader failures as \"read file body\" errors.","Validation and source-reader error tests required by the contract are absent."],"risks_b":["Upload duplicates Add’s option, request, response-decoding, and error logic instead of calling Add, creating avoidable semantic-drift risk and violating an explicit contract requirement.","The retry test uses strings.NewReader rather than a genuinely non-replayable streamed source such as an os.File or io.NopCloser.","Required tests for validation and source-reader failures are missing."]}
